fo:block.fo:block: Foreword

The International Organization of Legal Metrology (OIML) is an intergovernmental treaty organization whose primary aim is to harmonise the regulations and metrological controls applied by its Member States to measuring instruments used in trade, health, safety, and environmental protection.

This document, OIML X 999:2026, specifies how OIML publications are encoded in NISO STS (ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022). It is a derivative work: it draws its structure and most of its normative content from the ISO STS Guidelines for coding ed.2.1 and adapts that material to OIML’s publication context.
This first edition of OIML X 999 was approved by the OIML Technical Assembly in 2026. == Introduction

OIML publications are currently authored in Metanorma AsciiDoc (using the metanorma-​oiml flavor) and rendered to multiple output formats. To enable OIML publications to participate in the wider NISO STS ecosystem — the vocabulary used by ISO, IEC, NISO, and many national standards bodies — this document defines OIML’s profile of NISO STS 1.2.
This document is intended for:
authors and editors preparing OIML publications for publication in NISO STS;
tooling engineers building validation and rendering pipelines against OIML NISO STS XML; and
anyone consuming OIML publications in NISO STS who needs to understand the encoding conventions.
The document is normative where it says so. Where it is silent, NISO STS applies unchanged. == Scope
This document specifies the encoding of OIML publications in NISO STS (ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022).

It applies to all OIML document types — International Recommendations ®, International Basic Publications (B), International Documents (D), International Guides (G), and Expert Reports (E) — and to every publication stage from working draft through published edition.
It does not apply to:
OIML administrative or procedural documents that are not published in the OIML document series;
non-XML representations of OIML publications (e.g. derived PDF or HTML renderings);
vocabularies other than NISO STS 1.2.
Where this document is silent, NISO STS 1.2 applies unchanged. == Normative references

The following documents are referred to in the text in such a way that some or all of their content constitutes requirements of this document. For dated references, only the edition cited applies. For undated references, the latest edition of the referenced document (including any amendments) applies.
ANSI/NISO Z39.102-2022, STS: Standards Tag Suite (Version 1.2). NISO.
OIML B 6-2, Directives of the OIML — Guide 2: Preparation of OIML Recommendations and Documents.
ISO 30042, TermBase eXchange (TBX) — Machine-readable terminology interchange format.
RFC 3986, Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax. IETF, 2005.
BCP 47, Tags for Identifying Languages. IETF.

fo:block.fo:inline: The NISO STS Tag Library is the authoritative reference for the meaning of every NISO STS element and attribute used in this document. Where this document refers to an element by name (e.g. <std>), the corresponding chapter in the Tag Library is the normative definition.

fo:block.fo:block: 1​Terms and definitions

International Organization of Legal Metrology — the publisher of this document.

an OIML informative document published with the identifier form OIML D <num>:​<year>.

an OIML informative document published with the identifier form OIML E <num>:​<year>. =​= OIML profile

This clause defines OIML’s profile of NISO STS 1.2. The profile is intentionally minimal: OIML adopts the base vocabulary unchanged and adds only the conventions needed to identify OIML publications, support OIML’s bilingual (English + French) publishing model, and apply OIML editorial policy.

fo:block.fox:title: Section 2 ​ OIML constraints over base NISO STS
fo:block.fo:block: 2​OIML constraints over base NISO STS
OIML adds three constraints over base NISO STS 1.2. Each is normative.
2.1​Reused content shall carry <permission>
Any content reused by OIML from a source outside the OIML publication shall carry a <permission> element identifying the copyright holder and the license under which the content is reused.

Why: OIML’s editorial policy requires that readers can identify the provenance and license of every reused passage. NISO STS permits but does not require <permission>; OIML makes it mandatory for reused content.

fo:block.fo:inline: ”Reused content” includes quotations, figures, tables, code samples, and any other material that OIML did not author. Content authored by OIML does not require <permission>.

fo:block.fo:block: 2.2​<self-​uri> shall not occur inside <self-​xref>
The <self-​uri> element shall not occur as a descendant of <self-​xref>. The @​rid attribute of <self-​xref> is the only mechanism OIML permits for self-references inside an OIML publication.

Why: OIML’s rendering pipeline uses @​rid to resolve internal cross references at parse time; permitting <self-​uri> inside <self-​xref> introduces two resolution paths and causes ambiguous link targets.
2.3​Every <std> shall carry <title> and <pub-​date>
Every <std> element shall contain both <title> and <pub-​date>.
Why: OIML bibliographic tooling renders citations by concatenating <title> and <pub-​date>; omitting either element produces a malformed citation. == Document structure

An OIML publication encoded in NISO STS is rooted at the <standard> element (or <adoption> for publications adopted from another SDO). The root contains three peer blocks plus an optional processing-metadata block:

fo:block.font-family: Courier New, Noto Sans Mono, Noto Sans Mono CJK HK, Noto Sans Mono CJK JP, Noto Sans Mono CJK KR, Noto Sans Mono CJK SC, Noto Sans Mono CJK TC

fo:block.fo:block: 2.4​Front matter

The OIML front matter contains an <iso-​meta> block (used for compatibility with the wider STS ecosystem, even though OIML is not ISO), a foreword, and an introduction. For bilingual OIML publications, the secondary-language translation is carried in a sibling <iso-​meta xml:​lang=​"fr"> block. See Clause 3 for the required metadata fields.
2.5​Body

The body is built from nested <sec> elements. OIML clauses follow the standard ISO/IEC structure (Scope, Normative references, Terms and definitions, …, main clauses, Annexes). Each <sec> carries a <label> and a <title>.

fo:block.fo:inline: OIML uses arbitrary (non-semantic) @​id values for sections; the prior convention of semantic identifiers is being phased out — see the source coding guidelines §3.4.

fo:block.fo:block: 2.6​Back matter
The OIML back matter holds:
Annexes inside an <app-​group>; each annex is an <app> with @​content-​type of informative or normative.
The bibliography in a <ref-​list> with @​content-​type=​"bibliography".
Indexes (optional) using <index-​div> and <index-​entry>.
Footnotes in OIML publications live at the point of use, not in <back> — see Clause 7.

fo:block.fox:title: Section 4 ​ Body content
fo:block.fo:block: 4​Body content
This clause specifies OIML’s conventions for prose content in the body of a publication.
4.1​Paragraphs

Use

for paragraphs. OIML does not permit block-level structures inside

; nested structures must be siblings.
4.2​Lists
Use <list> with one of these @​list-​type values:
bullet — unordered list.
order — numbered list with Arabic numerals.
alpha-​lower, alpha-​upper — alphabetical.
roman-​lower, roman-​upper — Roman numerals.
arabic — added in NISO STS 1.2 for Arabic-numeral lists that do not fit order.

fo:block.fo:inline: OIML harmonises with ISO/IEC: the closed @​list-​type value list is the only permitted set (see the Coding Changes ed 2.1, §5.7).

fo:block.fo:block: Each <list-​item> may carry a <label>.
4.3​Tables
Tables are wrapped in <table-​wrap>. OIML uses the XHTML table model (<table> with <tr>, <td>, <th>) by default. The model in use is declared on <processing-​meta> via @​table-​model.
Table headers use <th> with <bold> for emphasis (harmonised with IEC practice from ed. 2.1).
For detailed table-coding rules, see the source coding guidelines Annex B.
4.4​Figures
Figures are wrapped in <fig> with a <label>, <caption>, and one or more <graphic> elements. OIML requires <alt-​text> on every figure for accessibility.
4.5​Quotations
Block quotations use <disp-​quote>. In NISO STS 1.2 (and OIML by extension), <disp-​quote> may carry a source (<attrib>) and usage permissions (<permissions>).
4.6​Notes and examples
OIML uses both normative and informative variants:
<normative-​note>, <non-​normative-​note>.
<normative-​example>, <non-​normative-​example>.
Notes inside tables, figures, and formulae use <table-​wrap-​foot> or <caption> as appropriate.
4.7​Code and preformatted text
Block code uses <code> with @​code-​type and @​xml:​space=​"preserve". Inline code uses <inline-​code> (NISO STS 1.2). Verbatim text that is not code uses <preformat>.

fo:block.fox:title: Section 5 ​ References and bibliography
fo:block.fo:block: 5​References and bibliography
OIML publications carry two reference lists in the back matter.
5.1​Normative references

Encoded as a <ref-​list> with @​content-​type=​"normative-​refs", typically inside <front> or as the first item in <back>. Each reference is held in a <ref> element wrapping a <mixed-​citation> or <element-​citation>.
5.2​Bibliography
Encoded as a <ref-​list> with @​content-​type=​"bibliography" in <back>.
5.3​Citing other standards
References to other standards use the <std> element inside the citation. OIML places the following constraints over base NISO STS:
Every <std> shall carry both <title> and <pub-​date>. See Clause 2.
<std> may carry @​use-​type to indicate whether the reference is dated, undated, or qualified (NISO STS 1.2 addition).
5.4​Citing OIML’s own publications
When an OIML publication cites another OIML publication, the <std> element’s <std-​ident> child carries:
<std-​org> with content OIML.
<std-​id> with the OIML identifier (e.g., OIML R 7:​1979).
<doc-​identifier> mirroring the same.

fo:block.fo:inline: OIML does not use punctuation between elements in <ref-​list> — this is harmonised with the IEC practice from ed. 2.1 (see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §4.4.2).

fo:block.fox:title: Section 6 ​ Mathematics, figures, and tables
fo:block.fo:block: 6​Mathematics, figures, and tables
6.1​Mathematics
Inline mathematics use <inline-​formula>; display (block) mathematics use <disp-​formula>. OIML requires MathML 3.0 (declared on <processing-​meta> via @​mathml=​"MathML 3.​0").

fo:block.font-family: Courier New, Noto Sans Mono, Noto Sans Mono CJK HK, Noto Sans Mono CJK JP, Noto Sans Mono CJK KR, Noto Sans Mono CJK SC, Noto Sans Mono CJK TC

fo:block.fo:block: A formula key (legend) uses the <legend> element (NISO STS 1.2 addition — see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §7.3).
6.2​Figures
Figures follow the conventions in [_body_content]. The size of a graphic may be indicated in @​specific-​use (NISO STS 1.2 — see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §5.10).

Unit statements in figures: in OIML, the

containing the unit statement lives inside the figure caption () — harmonised with ed. 2.1 §8.4.
Sub-figures and multiple graphics: see the source coding guidelines §8.2 for the conventions OIML adopts.
6.3​Tables

OIML tables use the XHTML table model by default. The full table-coding conventions (alignment, merged cells, line breaks, lists inside cells, landscape tables, rules, frames, border styling, alignment of the table, text rotation) are inherited from the source coding guidelines Annex B.

fo:block.fo:inline: OIML harmonises with ISO/IEC ed. 2.1 on table styling (see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §6.3). Tables may carry size attributes for rendering information (see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §6.1).

fo:block.fox:title: Section 7 ​ Indexing and navigation
fo:block.fo:block: 7​Indexing and navigation
7.1​Tables of contents
The table of contents is generated from the section structure; it is not authored by hand. OIML rendering tooling produces the TOC from <sec>/<app> <label> and <title> pairs.
For author-controlled navigation aids (e.g., lists of figures, lists of tables), use a <list-​of> element with the appropriate @​list-​type.
7.2​Indexes
An author-created subject index lives in <back> inside an <index-​div> tree. Each <index-​entry> carries a <term> and optional <see> or <see-​also> cross references, plus a target pointer (<xref>).
7.3​Internal cross-references
Internal cross-references use <xref> with @​rid pointing at the target’s @​id. The @​ref-​type attribute identifies the kind of target. OIML permits these @​ref-​type values:
sec — section.
table — table.
fig — figure.
fn — footnote.
bibr — bibliographic entry.
abbreviation — abbreviation (added in NISO STS 1.2; replaces the earlier @​ref-​type=​"other" practice).
custom — with @​custom-​type of note, term-​entry, or example (added in NISO STS 1.2).

For self-references within an OIML publication, the <self-​xref> element is used; OIML resolves self-references via the @​rid attribute only — see Clause 2 for the OIML-specific prohibition on <self-​uri> inside <self-​xref>.
7.4​Footnotes
Footnote text in OIML lives at the point of use (inside the <fn> element), not collected in <back>. This is harmonised with the IEC practice from ed. 2.1 (see Coding Changes ed 2.1, §10.1.8).

fo:block.fo:block: 8.3​Identifier mapping

OIML identifiers (OIML R <num>:​<year>, etc.) are passed through verbatim. The OIML document-type letter (R, B, D, G, E, X) is encoded as a <custom-​meta> with @​meta-​name=​"oiml-​doc-​series" inside <iso-​meta>.

The output OIML NISO STS XML SHALL satisfy the constraints in Clause 2. The converter SHALL emit <permission> on any reused content marked in the source, SHALL NOT emit <self-​uri> inside <self-​xref>, and SHALL emit <title> and <pub-​date> on every <std>.
